question:
If $f(x)$ is continuous and differentiable in $x \in [-7, 0]$ and $f'(x) \le 2 \forall x \in [-7, 0]$, also $f(-7) = -3$ then range of $f(-1) + f(0)$
यदि $f(x), x \in [-7, 0]$ में सतत् तथा अवकलनीय है तथा $f'(x) \le 2 \forall x \in [-7, 0]$ और $f(-7) = -3$ तो $f(-1) + f(0)$ का परिसर है-
explanation:
Lets use LMVT for $x \in [-7, -1]$ में लांग्राज मध्यमान प्रमेय से
$\frac{f(-1) - f(-7)}{(-1 + 7)} \le 2$
$\frac{f(-1) + 3}{6} \le 2 \Rightarrow f(-1) \le 9$
Also use LMVT for $x \in [-7, 0]$ में लांग्राज मध्यमान प्रमेय से
$\frac{f(0) - f(-7)}{(0 + 7)} \le 2$
$\frac{f(0) + 3}{7} \le 2 \Rightarrow f(0) \le 11$
$\therefore f(0) + f(-1) \le 20$
subject: Mathematics

question: The statement $(p \rightarrow (q \rightarrow p)) \rightarrow (p \rightarrow (p \vee q))$ is
explanation:
Let's simplify $(p \rightarrow (q \rightarrow p)) \rightarrow (p \rightarrow (p \vee q))$
Note that $q \rightarrow p \equiv \sim q \vee p$, so $p \rightarrow (q \rightarrow p) \equiv p \rightarrow (\sim q \vee p) \equiv \sim p \vee (\sim q \vee p) = T$.
Thus the statement becomes $T \rightarrow (p \rightarrow (p \vee q))$.
Since $p \vee q$ is always true when $p$ is true, $p \rightarrow (p \vee q)$ is $T$.
Thus $T \rightarrow T \equiv T$, which is a tautology.
